tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Blythewater Marine** provides vessel tracking and port logistics services to shipping operators across northern Europe. The company runs a hub-and-spoke network in the North Europe region.

**Current Environment:**
- Hub virtual network **VNet-Hub** (10.60.0.0/16) contains a VPN gateway named **VGW-Hub** with an active site-to-site tunnel to the harbor headquarters
- Spoke virtual network **VNet-Ops** (10.61.0.0/16) is peered with VNet-Hub and contains the subnet **Subnet-Ingest** with 60 Linux VMs that process vessel telemetry
- Field surveyors work from laptops aboard vessels and in remote ports, connecting over whatever internet access is available

**Business Requirements:**
- Outbound connectivity from Subnet-Ingest must be reliable at peak load and present a small, fixed set of source IP addresses to external partners
- The company wants exactly **one** VPN gateway in the whole topology; spokes must not get their own gateways
- Surveyor remote access must authenticate with corporate Microsoft Entra ID identities and be subject to Conditional Access with multifactor authentication

tabs.title: Networking Detail
tabs.content:
**Telemetry Egress (Subnet-Ingest):**
- The 60 VMs continuously call a partner tide-data API on the internet; the partner allowlists at most **four** source IP addresses per customer
- During peak processing windows, outbound connections from the subnet intermittently fail; diagnostics point to exhaustion of source network address translation (SNAT) ports on the default outbound access path
- No inbound connections from the internet to the VMs are required

**Headquarters Reachability:**
- Servers at the harbor headquarters must reach the VMs in VNet-Ops through the existing tunnel terminated on VGW-Hub in the hub
- Currently, headquarters servers can reach hub resources but **cannot** reach any spoke address; the VNet-Hub / VNet-Ops peering is configured with default settings on both sides

**Surveyor Remote Access:**
- Surveyors will use the Azure VPN Client on company Windows laptops
- Sign-in must use Microsoft Entra ID credentials (no client certificates to manage) so that Conditional Access and MFA policies apply
- Some vessel and port networks are known to block classic IPsec/IKE ports, so the tunnel should work over standard outbound TLS (TCP 443)
